variables.content: The best Chern-insulator design obtained (SG 168, $C_z=1$, HS gap 5.1% equaling full-BZ gap) is claimed to have the largest known complete bandgap of any three-dimensional photonic Chern insulator in the literature surveyed, and it achieves this without employing supercell modulation techniques used in earlier proposals.
variables.title: Claimed record: largest-known complete bandgap for a 3D photonic Chern insulator (author assertion)

variables.content: A top-down, inverse design method based on density-based topology optimization is introduced for synthesizing acoustic topological insulators. The approach directly targets backscattering-protected, directional energy transport by maximizing transmission to two output ports and minimizing transmission to a third, without imposing any explicit requirements on the existence of pseudospin-1/2 edge states, the Chern numbers of the topological phases, or band symmetry inversion. These topological properties emerge spontaneously during the optimization process.
variables.title: Inverse design method for acoustic TIs

variables.content: The overlapped band gap between the optimized nontrivial PC (NP1) and trivial PC (TP) achieves a width of 29.3% (normalized frequency range $\Omega=0.434$ to $0.583$), which is more than twice that of the existing SPTI designs reported in Refs. [28,29,31].
variables.title: Overlapped band gap of 29.3%, more than twice that of existing SPTIs

variables.content: The inverse design of a topological waveguide is formulated as a paired-unit-cell optimization over design vectors \boldsymbol{d}^{(1)} and \boldsymbol{d}^{(2)}, where each \boldsymbol{d}^{(i)}=(x_{0}^{(i)},\rho_{1}^{(i)},\rho_{2}^{(i)},\rho_{3}^{(i)},\rho_{4}^{(i)},\phi^{(i)})^{\top} is constrained to an admissible set and the objective enforces opposite predicted labels ψ^{(1)}=-1 and ψ^{(2)}=+1 together with maximizing or targeting the normalized width of their common nontrivial bandgap; in this formulation the learned maps \mathcal{F}_c:\boldsymbol{d}\mapsto\psi (the trained classification network) and \mathcal{F}_r:\boldsymbol{d}\mapsto(\bar{\omega}_1,\bar{\omega}_2) (the trained regression network) are substituted for direct topology and band-structure computations inside the optimization constraints.
variables.title: Optimization formulation for paired MMC unit cells using learned surrogates

variables.content: The presented two-step inverse-design approach directly generates a pair of unit cells (a first unit cell (FUC) and a counterpart unit cell (CUC)) with distinct topological characters for both acoustic and electromagnetic waves and explicitly maximizes their bandgap matching, rather than relying on parameter scans across a single Dirac-point band inversion to choose unit cells before and after a phase transition. This direct-pair construction workflow produces practical phoxonic topological insulator (PxTI) interfaces without requiring the pre-identification of critical band-inversion points.
variables.title: Direct unit cell pair generation approach distinct from band-inversion selection

variables.content: Maximizing the common bandgap width $G_{4,5}$ for the fourth–fifth band pair in the inverse design yields a relative bandgap that is approximately 70% larger than the common bandgap computed for the manually designed valley‑like structure reported by Xia et al., Phys. Rev. B 97, 155124 (2018); the reported numerical improvement is therefore a pairwise comparison against that single prior design.
variables.title: ~70% wider common bandgap versus the Xia et al. 2018 design

variables.content:
In the modified Qi-Wu-Zhang model with open boundary conditions in the \(x\)-direction and periodic in the \(y\)-direction, implemented on a lattice of width \(L_x\) with Hamiltonian \(H_{\mathrm{op}}(k_y)\) (given explicitly in the model definition), the smooth width-modulation procedure—adding the edge potential
      \[
      H_{\mathrm{edge}}(u)=\left(|1\rangle\langle 1|+|L_x\rangle\langle L_x|\right)\otimes \tan\!\left(\frac{\pi u}{2}\right)\sigma_z,\quad u\in[0,1),
      \]
      and then repeating on the new edges—continuously reduces the effective width from \(L_x\) to \(L_x-2\). By iterating this procedure, the width can be reduced stepwise; for example, from \(L_x=20\) down to \(L_x=6\). Tracking the centers of the several rightmost spectral gaps as \(u\) increases shows that these gaps never close during the modulation. Consequently, the system can be taken continuously from an effectively two-dimensional Chern insulator (large \(L_x\)) to an effectively one-dimensional topological insulator (small \(L_x\)) along a path that does not close the energy gap separating occupied and unoccupied states.
variables.title: Existence of a continuous gapped path between two-dimensional and one-dimensional topological phases

variables.content: Ordinary lattice defects provide a generic and practical mechanism to localize mid-gap modes that diagnose band topology or local topological changes, as demonstrated by model studies and acoustic-lattice experiments on the Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) Chern insulator. These findings should be pertinent across lattice symmetries and physical dimensions and can be exploited to (a) trap localized Majorana modes near ordinary defects in topological superconductors (with suitable spinor redefinitions of the QWZ model to $p+ip$ pairing contexts), and (b) motivate ordinary-defect-engineered topological devices in metamaterials (acoustic, photonic, phononic, and topoelectric circuits), as well as motivate analogous studies in Floquet and non-Hermitian lattices (including defect-localized non-Hermitian skin effects).
variables.title: Ordinary defects as generic probes of topology with applications to Majorana trapping and topological devices

variables.content: The coupled trilayer Chern system, composed of three Qi-Wu-Zhang layers with Chern numbers $C_1=+1$, $C_2=-1$, $C_3=+1$ in the decoupled limit and with interlayer tunneling $t_\perp$, realizes a two-dimensional hybrid-order topological insulator. In this phase, a single chiral edge mode and a pair of zero-dimensional corner states coexist within the same bulk gap.
variables.title: Realization of 2D hybrid-order topological insulator in coupled trilayer Chern system

variables.content:
A continuous deformation connects a minimal two-band Chern insulator to a higher-order skin effect (HOSE) phase: the two-band Bloch Hamiltonian
      $h_{\mathrm{def}}^{\mathrm{Re}}(\mathbf{k})=\sin k_{x}\,\sigma_{x}+\sin k_{y}\,\sigma_{y}+(m+t\cos k_{x}+\cos k_{y})\sigma_{z}+\mathrm{i}\cos k_{x}(1-g)\,\sigma_{0}$,
      where $\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z}$ are the Pauli matrices and $\sigma_{0}$ is the $2\times2$ identity matrix, with parameter path $(g,t)=(1,1)-\theta(1,1)$ for $\theta:0\to1$ (mass $m$ fixed at $0.5$), transforms the Hermitian Qi-Wu-Zhang Chern-insulator regime at $(g,t)=(1,1)$ into a HOSE regime at $(g,t)=(0,0)$. Along this deformation (i) a bulk phase transition occurs where a line gap closes and the bulk Chern number changes (the strong bulk topology becomes trivial), and (ii) one pair of chiral edge bands detaches from the bulk and becomes spectrally isolated as point-gapped edge bands that wind in the complex-energy plane; the winding on that one pair of opposite edges yields an $O(L)$ corner skin effect under full open boundary conditions.
variables.title: Continuous deformation of a two-band Chern insulator into a HOSE phase

variables.content:
For the two-band Qi–Wu–Zhang Chern-insulator ramp that crosses the isolated gap-closing cone at momentum $\mathbf{k}_c=(0,0)$ and critical parameter $m_c=-2$, the leading-order momentum-resolved probability to excite from the lower to the upper band in the slow-parameter-ramp limit is given by the Landau–Zener expression
      $$
      P_{\mathrm{LZ}}^{\mathbf{k}}\approx\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi \mathbf{k}^2}{v_{\mathrm{LZ}}}\right),
      $$
      where the two-dimensional momentum $\mathbf{k}$ is measured relative to the gap-closing momentum $\mathbf{k}_c$, and the effective Landau–Zener velocity is the instantaneous slope of the mass parameter at the crossing time,
      $$
      v_{\mathrm{LZ}}=\big|\dot{m}(t_c)\big|=v\,\big|m_f+2\big|
      $$
      for the exponential ramp $m(t)=m_f-(m_f-m_i)e^{-v t}$ that crosses $m_c=-2$; here $v>0$ is the scalar ramp parameter and $m_i,m_f$ are the initial and final mass values. This Gaussian-in-$\mathbf{k}$ profile sets the leading spatial profile of excitations created in the nonadiabatic crossing and controls the narrowness of the excitation region in momentum space.
variables.title: Landau–Zener excitation probability for Dirac cone crossing

variables.content: The nontrivial band gap $\Delta$ of the quantum well (QW) formed by a single graphene layer sandwiched between two single quintuple-layer (QL) slabs of Bi2Se3 is tunable by varying the interlayer distance and the thickness of the Bi2Se3 cladding: (a) compressing the interlayer distance between graphene and the Bi2Se3 QLs increases the hybridization and increases $\Delta$ from $\sim 30\ \mathrm{meV}$ (equilibrium) to $\sim 50\ \mathrm{meV}$ at an interlayer compression of $0.45\ \mathrm{\AA}$, corresponding to a nominal applied pressure of $3.78\ \mathrm{GPa}$; (b) increasing the Bi2Se3 slab thickness beyond a single QL reduces the QW energy gap, and when each cladding reaches 3 QLs the gap closes due to the emergence of gapless three-dimensional topological surface states. Thus, $1\ \mathrm{QL}$ Bi2Se3 cladding and controlled interlayer separation provide the optimal parameter regime for achieving the largest, intrinsic two-dimensional topological insulator (2D TI) gap in this design.
variables.title: Tunability of the nontrivial quantum-well band gap in the Bi2Se3/graphene/Bi2Se3 quantum well by interlayer compression and cladding thickness

variables.content: The Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) Chern insulator model under an irrational magnetic flux (with flux per unit cell β = (√5-1)/2) reduces to a one-dimensional spinor quasiperiodic chain with onsite matrix potential controlled by the hopping amplitude t_x (quasiperiodic modulation strength), intercell hopping t_y (set to 1 in numerical calculations), and topological mass m. The eigenstate transitions depend on the relative magnitudes of |m+2| and t_y. When |m+2| > t_y, increasing t_x produces the conventional extended-critical-localized sequence with a critical line at t_x = t_y. When |m+2| ≤ t_y, the system undergoes an extended-to-critical transition at t_x = |m+2| and remains in a critical phase for all t_x ≥ |m+2|, without entering a localized phase even for arbitrarily strong quasiperiodic modulation.

related.content: The magnetic Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) model (a two-dimensional Chern insulator under an irrational magnetic flux, reduced to a one-dimensional spinor quasiperiodic chain) possesses a dual transformation that exchanges the hopping amplitudes t_x and t_y (along with the corresponding Bloch phases k_x and k_y). Under this transformation, the real-space Hamiltonian maps to a momentum-space Hamiltonian of identical form. Consequently, the real-space phase diagram maps to the momentum-space phase diagram with extended and localized regions exchanged, while critical regions remain delocalized in both representations.
related.title: Dual transformation exchanging t_x and t_y

variables.title: Eigenstate transitions in the magnetic QWZ model

variables.content: The two principal phenomena — the subband-count formula $N=|q-C|$ and the emergence of anomalous open-orbit subbands with Chern numbers $q-1$ and $-q-1$ — are observed in numerical Hofstadter spectra of multiple lattice Chern-insulator models: the Qi–Wu–Zhang model, the Haldane model, and higher-Chern-number tight-binding constructions. This cross-model verification indicates the phenomena are not artifacts of a single fine-tuned model but are robust features tied to parent-band topology and saddle-point structure.

related.content: For Bloch bands of Chern insulators at rational flux $\phi/\phi_{0}=p/q$ (here $p/q=1/q$ in the computed examples), the parent band splits into $N=|q-C|$ magnetic subbands, where $C$ is the Chern number of the parent (zero-field) band and $q$ is the flux-denominator integer. This counting was observed numerically in Hofstadter spectra of the Qi–Wu–Zhang (QWZ) model (examples at $q=4$) and in higher-Chern-number models (examples at $q=8$).
related.title: Parent band splits into $N=|q-C|$ magnetic subbands at rational flux $\phi/\phi_0=p/q$

variables.title: Two principal phenomena verified across QWZ, Haldane, and higher-Chern-number models

variables.content: The slab-phase diagram of the non-Hermitian model \(H_3 = H_0 + i t_1 \sin k_x \sigma_z\) (with \(H_0\) the Qi-Wu-Zhang model, in the first quadrant \(m>0, t_1>0\)) is mirror-symmetric about \(m=1\) and comprises six regions: a trivial gapped phase T with line gap and Chern number \(0\); two gapped topological regions \(C_{1}^{LR}\) and \(C_{1}^{LL}\), each with band Chern numbers \(\pm1\) but differing in that \(C_{1}^{LR}\) has one edge mode on each edge while \(C_{1}^{LL}\) has both edge modes on the left edge; and three gapless regions \(GL_1\), \(GL_2\), and \(S'\), where \(S'\) is a topological gapless membrane phase with edge modes traversing a hole in the continuum bands.

related.content:
For the non-Hermitian model \(H_2 = H_0 + i h_x \sigma_x\) with \(H_0\) the Qi-Wu-Zhang model, in the slab geometry (open boundaries in \(x\), periodic in \(y\), in the thermodynamic limit \(L\to\infty\)), the continuum bands are obtained from the analytically continued Hamiltonian \(\mathcal{H}_2(\beta,k_y)\) (obtained by \(e^{ik_x}\to\beta\)) with \(\beta\) on the GBZ. These continuum bands define three distinct slab phases in the first quadrant \(m>0, h_x>0\): two gapped topological phases \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) with line gaps and band Chern numbers \(\pm1\) and \(\pm2\) respectively, and a gapless topological slab phase \(S\). All slab-phase boundaries, where the continuum-band line gap closes, are given analytically by the four curves on the \((m,h_x)\) plane
      $$
      m=\sqrt{1+h_x^2}\pm 1,\qquad h_x=\sqrt{(m\mp1)^2+1},
      $$
      i.e. the set \(\{m=\sqrt{1+h_x^2}+1,\; m=\sqrt{1+h_x^2}-1,\; h_x=\sqrt{(m-1)^2+1},\; h_x=\sqrt{(m+1)^2+1}\}\).
related.title: Analytic slab phase boundaries and three slab phases for H2

variables.title: Slab phase diagram of H3 with six regions and mirror symmetry about m=1
